answer: Each AI agent must lock a ferrous‑valued bond in a distributed ledger, which emits a cryptographic signal each epoch proving continued participation. Peers in the orchard of validators periodically broadcast zero‑knowledge proofs that the bonded identity behaved correctly; any mismatch triggers an automatic slash of the bond. An attacker therefore must acquire enough ferrous stake to spin up many identities and pay the slash cost for each falsified proof, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
